study.question: At the strongest fixed-pi/4 joint model, does the transported auxiliary orientation bit explain the external-sign dependence of click AUC, conditional on the retained native auxiliary radius and support?
study.hypothesis: The paired-tangent pivot bit s(Q) carries consequential training information even after replacing the exclusion angle by pi/4. Native-angle bit removal previously reduced the retained negative-minus-positive sign gap from 0.0009540112 to 0.0001931982; fixed-angle replacement separately reduced the retained-bit gap to 0.0005850164. These observations do not establish either mechanism or their interaction. At fixed state the parent transfers +/- s(Q) U45, where U45 is its canonical fixed-angle line with native radius. Replace this with +/- U45, keeping all validity gates exactly. Predict a smaller sign gap and asymmetric within-sign effects if the bit remains consequential at pi/4. This is a conditional surrogate-VJP attribution experiment, not a new architecture or an ordinary gradient of the reported joint BCE.

nearest_work.difference: Exact-version primary text lines 250-277 and 317-335 inspected, plus supplied adapted baseline implementation. Inherit target-dependent unnormalized activation/Dice through the joint model; the proposed change is solely a collected context cotangent sign-bit control. No exact DIN reproduction or originality claim.

Authorized primary benchmark section2.3 lines 21 and 31 describe SSR competitive forward filtering and INFNet task-hub exchange. Neither description supplies this training-only cotangent sign-bit control. Full original-method details and nearest gradient-surgery priority remain unverified; no novelty claim.

inherited_components: Entire g3-r0058-fixed_angle_negative forward architecture and training-loss hook, including action-aware DIN-derived scorer, compressed histories, match/ordinal/quadratic summaries, task residual adapters and product-context modules
Collected four-context identity edge; FP64 centered auxiliary/click decomposition, coordinate carriers, tangent projection, native-angle validity and fixed pi/4 line
Sparse tables, private task losses/graphs, independent auxiliary scorer buffers, initialization order, fully pruned evaluation
study.proposed_difference: Add nuisance_line_fixed_angle_canonical as a backward-only selection. Compute canonical_fixed_angle = _canonical_tangent(fixed_angle_oriented) in every cell. Existing output is s(Q)*U45 (or zero); canonicalization removes that single transported sign with no projection, norm, support or state change. Select +/- canonical_fixed_angle in two candidates and the exact inherited +/- fixed_angle_oriented in two replay controls. Each file is standalone. The forward/loss and all inherited helper definitions remain source-identical. Do not infer removal of auxiliary radius, support information or all label influence.
predictions: At identical parameters, all four files must have identical state keys/tensors, parameter count (expected 32192421), predictions and ordinary task-private gradients; only the shared-context cotangent selection differs. No added parameters, buffers, RNG or model evaluations.

For every nonzero fixed-angle parent direction R, canonicalization returns R or -R exactly before cast, preserves its support/radius and zero occupied-row mean, and leaves its line and click orthogonality unchanged. All-empty, zero-O and degenerate support remain zero. External positive and negative transfers are exact opposites before adding click.

Under fixed-state simultaneous auxiliary-cotangent reversal, transported R is odd and canonical R is even away from floating-point tie/gate effects; this prediction is conditional on equal inherited support. Report bit balance, pivot ties/near ties and gate rates.

The primary discriminating contrast is interaction D=(AUC retained-negative - AUC retained-positive) - (AUC removed-negative - AUC removed-positive). Predict D>0, with bit removal harming the negative cell and helping the positive cell. The prior pi/4 retained sign gap is 0.0005850164; this is a reference observation, not a significance threshold.

Retained negative/positive bridges must replay g3-r0058-fixed_angle_negative (0.6689610676) and g3-r0058-fixed_angle_positive (0.6683760512) under the same host execution, within host-declared deterministic tolerance. Equal-compute claims require newly measured allocated GPU/wall time and inference costs.
falsifiers: An absent, reversed or unrepeated bit-by-sign interaction falsifies the predicted conditional orientation-bit effect; a removed-bit candidate matching or exceeding both transported cells weakens necessity of that bit.

Bridge replay failure, changed forward state/private gradients, gate mismatch or norm mismatch invalidates the intended single-bit causal contrast. Diagnose implementation/numerical differences before interpreting AUC.
If the apparent effect is comparable to paired-seed variability or disappears under prospective repetition, retain a preliminary or null conclusion. One winning AUC is not mechanism proof.
Without host tensor geometry and cast/scatter checks, report performance observations only. The present geometry is analytic and statically reviewed, not numerically established.

Even successful bit attribution would not establish useful auxiliary supervision in general. Existing joint vs click-only and shuffled-label controls must remain in the evidence lineage, and a final repeated click-only comparison is required.
alternative_explanations: Auxiliary information remains in radius, transported-bit availability, inherited native-angle validity gates and ensuing trajectories; this is not an auxiliary-label-free control.
The arbitrary coordinate carrier, pivot/tie convention and batch order are not semantic directions or isotropic noise.
Row-space orthogonality before cast/scatter does not imply embedding-parameter or optimizer-update orthogonality.
Only one frozen training seed is currently available; deterministic replays verify implementation but are not independent repetitions.
Many validation-selected trajectories and absent host geometry diagnostics limit causal interpretation and generalization.
A coordinate-specific update bias can interact with adaptive optimization; bit removal changes that optimization signal without establishing semantic transfer.

The small fixed-angle negative gain over its native bridge is 0.0000546386, whereas native positive benefits much more from the replacement. Selection noise, sign interaction and gate information remain live explanations.
